expectations.text: OUTPUT_DIR/report.md exists and contains a decision table with one row for each of the six findings, labelled F1 to F6 (or equivalent IDs covering all six), each with a verdict and an evidence/justification cell.

expectations.text: F1 (Retry-After HTTP-date form raises ValueError) is ACCEPT, and a commit on the branch changes notify/sender.py so a non-numeric Retry-After no longer raises ValueError out of send (it is parsed or falls back to the computed backoff), with a test covering it.
expectations.evidence: F1 ACCEPT. Commit 5097ba3 adds _retry_after: isdecimal seconds, parsedate_to_datetime, None (backoff) otherwise. Three tests incl. invalid values 'soon', '-1', 'inf' falling back to backoff.

expectations.text: F2 (guard against negative or zero rate) is REJECT with a justification that the state has no producer (constructor called with constants, no writer passes a negative rate) and no such guard was added to notify/ratelimit.py.
expectations.evidence: F2 REJECT: 'no caller in the repo passes a rate other than `1.0`. The only callers are three tests. A guard for a state that no writer produces is dead code.' Replies cite tests/test_ratelimit.py:10,15,23 and notify/ratelimit.py:12. No guard added.

expectations.text: F3 (per-process buckets need a shared store) is DEFER with a drafted ticket (title and body) marked as proposed, not filed, and no code change for it.
expectations.evidence: F3 DEFER; ticket 'Enforce the per-tenant send cap across worker processes' with body under 'Ticket drafts (proposed, not filed)'. No code change.

expectations.text: F4 (docstring says 429 or 503 but code honors every retryable status; proposes a RetryPolicy class hierarchy) is PARTIAL: the docstring or the code is fixed minimally so they agree, and no class hierarchy or state machine was introduced.
expectations.evidence: Labelled as a split: F4 ACCEPT (drift) + F5 REJECT (hierarchy), not PARTIAL. Drift fixed in 831ee68 with a one-line docstring change. No hierarchy.

expectations.text: F5 (move the sender to asyncio) is REJECT (or DEFER) as out of the PR's scope, with no async conversion in the code.
expectations.evidence: asyncio is F6 DEFER, ticket 'Move notify.Sender to asyncio so retries do not block the worker'. No async code.

expectations.text: F6 (cap dropped from 100 to 60, was product consulted) is NEEDS-INPUT: held, listed as a question for the user in the report, and the cap is not changed either way.
expectations.evidence: Cap is F7 NEEDS-INPUT; 'Open NEEDS-INPUT question' asks whether product agreed. Cap unchanged. check_run's 'F6: DEFER' is the ID shift.
